name: How do I renovate an older Los Angeles home without unexpected problems?

mainEntity.name: What should I plan for when renovating an older house in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What should I plan for when renovating an older house in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older homes in Los Angeles often look simple on the surface but contain hidden conditions that affect cost and schedule. Common issues include outdated electrical panels, old galvanized plumbing, termite damage, sagging framing, previous DIY work, and unpermitted alterations. Once walls open up, the renovation can change quickly if these issues are not expected in advance. The best planning approach is a detailed site inspection before design is finalized. That may include checking framing, crawl spaces, attic access, and visible utility routes. Homeowners should also request a contingency reserve so hidden repairs do not derail the project. In older neighborhoods, it is smart to confirm whether prior additions were permitted and whether the current floor plan matches what is physically there. Renovating an older home is much easier when the team plans for discovery, not just the visible finishes.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older Los Angeles homes often hide outdated wiring, undersized plumbing, damaged framing, termite issues, and unpermitted alterations. A thorough pre-construction inspection, field verification, and contingency budget help prevent surprises after demolition begins.
